items.text: Denhardt, R. B. — Public Administration — a core source for the Traditional Public Administration, NPM, and New Public Service comparison in Unit I.
Rosenbloom, D. H. — Public Administration: Understanding Management, Politics and Law — standard source for the politics-administration and law-management-politics framing used throughout.
Henry, N. — Public Administration and Public Affairs.
Kennedy, C. H. — Bureaucracy in Pakistan — a key source for Pakistan-specific administrative history and civil service material in Units I and VIII.
Weber, M. — original source of the ideal-type bureaucracy framework in Unit II.
Taylor, F. W. — original source of scientific management, referenced in Unit II.
Wilson, W., and Goodnow, F. — associated with the classical politics-administration dichotomy referenced in Unit I.
The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan — essential primary source for institutional, federal, and provincial structure throughout Units VIII, IX, and XI.

segments.text: Note on sourcing: the concepts and frameworks in this chapter (Weberian bureaucracy, scientific management, human relations theory, public choice theory, the politics-administration dichotomy, NPM, New Public Service, governance theory, and the standard policy-cycle and results-chain frameworks) are long-established, widely taught concepts drawn from the standard textbooks listed above. Pakistan-specific institutional, legal, and statistical details change over time with legislation and policy; any such specific detail should be verified against current official sources (the Constitution, applicable statutes, and current government publications) before being relied upon, as this chapter itself repeatedly notes. # Governance & Public Policies
CSS/PMS Group III Optional Subject — Code 24, 100 marks

Governance & Public Policies examines how power is exercised, how institutions are held accountable, how policy is actually made and implemented, and how citizens, the bureaucracy, and different levels of government interact — with Pakistan serving as the central running application throughout the syllabus. This chapter shares substantial conceptual ground with the Public Administration chapter (both cover accountability, bureaucracy, and policy implementation), but approaches these topics through a distinctly governance-theoretic and comparative-institutional lens, with heavier emphasis on internationally comparable governance indicators and normative governance theory.

Anne Mette Kjaer’s Governance, Mark Bevir’s Encyclopedia of Governance, Hill and Hupe’s Implementing Public Policy, Kraft and Furlong’s Public Policy: Politics, Analysis, Alternatives, the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, and the World Bank’s Worldwide Governance Indicators documentation are the standard reference works behind this syllabus.
